stories.title: France, Spain race to contain fires before new heatwave
stories.summary: Firefighters in France and Spain have rushed to contain the worst wildfires in living memory, seizing crucial hours before the arrival of another wave of searing temperatures. Blazes have ripped through vast swathes of woodland in both countries, incinerating properties and forcing the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of people - residents and tourists alike. A large wildfire 15km from the outskirts of the French winemaking capital of Bordeaux created a rare pyrocumulonimbus cloud - a phenomenon that can create wind and lightning. In the southwestern city's surrounding Gironde region, tractors fitted with blades to clear land, pickups towing water tanks and logging trucks sped to join a convoy of fire engines yesterday.

stories.title: Flavio Bolsonaro to launch Brazil presidential candidacy
stories.summary: Battered by a string of political crises, Flavio Bolsonaro will today formally launch his candidacy for Brazil's October presidential election, seeking to follow in the footsteps of his father, Jair Bolsonaro. Far-right firebrand Jair Bolsonaro anointed his eldest son as his successor after being sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup in response to his defeat by leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Brazil's 2022 election. The Liberal Party (PL) will officially name senator Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, as its candidate at a convention in Sao Paulo, with Argentina's libertarian President Javier Milei as a guest of honor. Flavio Bolsonaro is promising change: he wants to "free" Brazil of crime, inflation, high taxes and Mr Lula, who is seeking a fourth term in office.

stories.title: Why an Irish semi-state body is cashing in on a satellite company
stories.summary: Analysis: You may never have heard of AirNav Ireland but its multi-million windfall is a useful reminder about Ireland's aviation influence Most people have never heard of AirNav Ireland, and fewer still know it owns a slice of a satellite company. That's about to change, at least for the accounts department. The semi-state company is set for a multimillion-euro windfall as US satellite operator Iridium buys out the stake it holds in Aireon, the company that tracks aircraft from space, in a deal worth roughly €321 million. Aireon runs the world's only space-based air traffic surveillance system, flying as a payload on Iridium's satellite constellation since 2019. Rather than relying on ground radar, which has gaps over oceans and remote regions, Aireon tracks aircraft everywhere on the planet using onboard transponder signals picked up from orbit. Iridium is buying the remaining 61% of Aireon it doesn't already own, for around $367 million, from NAV Canada, AirNav Ireland, Italy's ENAV, the UK's NATS and Denmark's Naviair. Half of this is paid on closing, the rest a year later and Iridium is also taking on roughly $155 million of Aireon's debt.

stories.title: Three dead after shooting at Seattle food festival
stories.summary: Three people have been killed and at least four others wounded, including a toddler, after an apparent gunfight near the Space Needle landmark in Seattle last night, according to police. Seattle Police said one suspect had been arrested and they were searching for another following the incident at the Bite of Seattle food festival in a popular tourist district of the northwestern US city. Assistant Police Chief Tyrone Davis said shots were heard around 6pm (2am Irish time) and "there were two people who we believe were shooting at each other." Two weapons were recovered. Seattle Police said two people died at the scene at the Seattle Center and a third died in hospital.

stories.title: Why teens struggle with anxiety, and how to help
stories.summary: Niamh Delmar is a Chartered Registered Counselling Psychologist, mental health writer, and media contributor. Counselling psychologist Niamh Delmar shares her tips for helping teens suffering from anxiety. Anxiety disorders among adolescents are on the increase globally. The World Health Organisation asserts that they are the most prevalent disorders among children and teens. Conditions include generalised anxiety disorder, social phobia, panic disorder, agoraphobia, separation anxiety and agoraphobia. It's not all in the head. The amygdala in the brain, which triggers the fear response, is hyperactivated. Symptoms involve excessive worry, significant distress and impaired daily functioning. Common signs are irritability, difficulty concentrating, obsessing, withdrawal, avoidance, seeking reassurance, sleep disturbance and a range of physical issues.

stories.summary: The Government has announced it is drafting a new National Parks Bill that would allow for by-laws prohibiting or restricting certain activities, like the use of disposable barbecues, alongside other sanctions, in the country's national parks. stories.title: Consumer sentiment slips in July on cost-of-living woes
stories.summary: Consumer sentiment fell slightly in July on concerns about the cost of living, the latest Credit Union Consumer Sentiment Survey shows today. The sentiment survey slipped to 61.6 in July from 62.2 in June. That is well below the long-term survey average of 83.2, but above a 40-month low of 53.3 hit in April following a sharp rise in fuel costs as a result of the Middle East conflict. Sub-indices measuring current conditions, consumer expectations and the economic outlook all fell slightly, the survey showed. "Concerns about the cost of living continue to outweigh all other economic issues," said Irish League of Credit Unions CEO David Malone.

stories.title: Rugby bodies seek to throw out concussion lawsuits
stories.summary: World Rugby and England and Wales' governing bodies have sought to throw out nearly 380 former rugby union players' lawsuits over neurological injuries, arguing their lawyers repeatedly failed to disclose key medical evidence. World Rugby, the Rugby Football Union and the Welsh Rugby Union are facing lawsuits from around 800 ex-amateur and professional players, who say repeated concussive and sub-concussive blows left them with serious neurological conditions. The claimants' lawyers allege the governing bodies breached their duty of care by failing to protect them from those risks, but World Rugby argues in its written defence that it had no such duty and that injuries are an "inherent risk" in rugby. The case began in 2022 but has been beset by delays over disclosure, as has a parallel action by ex-rugby league players.

stories.title: Ban this filth! The untold history of film censorship in Ireland
stories.summary: In The Opinion of the Censor is a new documentary telling the story of the Censorship of Films Act 1923 and how one canny term in that statute has allowed consecutive holders of the role of Film Censor to reflect the prevailing values of Irish society over the last 100 years. 'Pernicious literature is a poison which corrupts the heart and undermines virtue, but its dreadful havoc is outdistanced by the pernicious effects of the filthy picture screen' In 1923, the founding fathers of the newly independent Irish state certainly shared Fr. Paul’s concerns and they moved swiftly to address the dangers they felt cinema presented. The Censorship of Films Act 1923 was one of the earliest statutes to be enacted by the legislature – just a week after the first Finance Bill! Films could be cut or banned if, ‘in the opinion of the Censor’, they were ‘indecent, obscene, blasphemous’ or ‘subversive of public morality’. The phrase was astutely drafted: it meant whoever held the statutorily independent post at any given time thereafter was empowered to call the shots.

stories.title: Abbey Road photo exhibition to open in London in August
stories.summary: A new Abbey Road photography exhibition in London will explore "almost a century of music history". London's world-famous Abbey Road recording studio is synonymous with The Beatles, but it has also hosted acts including Pink Floyd, Oasis, Stevie Wonder, Frank Ocean, and Stormzy over the past 95 years. It is now also the focus of the exhibition Abbey Road: Reframed, which presents three interconnected perspectives: The Art of Recording, Iconic Image Makers, and the Abbey Road Music Photography Accelerator. Together, they explore the artistry in the recording process, celebrate the photographers whose work has shaped music culture, and champion the next generation of image-makers defining its future.

stories.title: A financial guide for going to college this autumn
stories.summary: With July nearly over, it is only a few short weeks until your son or daughter starts the third level journey to their preferred college and subject. Harvard, for example, costs over $150,000 for the privilege of their parchment. That loan is inbuilt with their mortgage/rent payments. Here in Ireland, we are a far cry from that, but planning for the financial change of going to university or college is still important.

The Department of Justice has declined to give a breakdown of applications coming from Gaza. Last year, 114 long-stay study visa applications were granted to Palestinians worldwide, and 22 refused.

stories.title: Occupied Territories Bill signed into law by President
stories.summary: The long-awaited bill banning goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied territories in Palestine has been signed into law, despite ongoing criticism it does not include a ban on services. President Catherine Connolly signed the Israeli Settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territory (Prohibition of Importation of Goods) Bill 2026 into law this afternoon. Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. More than 500,000 Israeli settlers live in the territory, excluding the annexed east Jerusalem, among some three million Palestinians, which is illegal under international law. The now-law is the Government's version of Independent senator Frances Black's original Occupied Territories Bill, which she first drew up almost a decade ago, in 2018.

stories.title: Mortgage lending continues to rise - BPFI
stories.summary: Irish mortgage lending is continuing on an upward trajectory, according to Banking and Payment Federation Ireland's (BPFI) latest figures. The data shows over 21,000 mortgages were drawn down in first half of this year valued at almost €6.8 billion . The value of first-time buyer (FTB) mortgage drawdowns rose by 10.5% year on year to €4.1 billion, the highest half year level since the data series began in 2003 On an annualised basis, the value of mortgage approvals reached €17.6 billion in the 12 months ending June 2026, the highest level since the data series began in 2011.

stories.title: Burnham meets Zelensky, pledges new drone jamming tech
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has held his first meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at a UK naval base, pledging new "Stone Cloak" jamming technology to help safeguard Ukraine's drones on the battlefield. The meeting on the dockside and on board an aircraft carrier in the southern city of Portsmouth was Mr Burnham's first bilateral with a foreign leader and comes ahead of a visit by Mr Zelensky to Washington on Tuesday aimed at ending the four-year war with Russia. "We are with Ukraine 100%. I am personally with you 100%, Mr President," Mr Burnham assured Mr Zelensky after the two men, both wearing similar dark casual clothes, shook hands on the dockside. Mr Zelensky thanked Mr Burnham for an "important signal of support" and said he had invited Mr Burnham to visit Ukraine, after the leaders spoke by phone within hours of the new prime minister taking office.

stories.title: Shamrock Rovers hunt another huge European turnaround
stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers v Ararat Armenia, Tallaght Stadium, 8pm Irish time For the second time in two weeks, Shamrock Rovers are in Tallaght requiring an epic European recovery. Stephen Bradley's men trounced Floriana 5-1 a fortnight ago having stumbled to a 2-0 loss in the first leg over in Malta. No League of Ireland team had previously overturned a two-goal, first-leg deficit in Europe but the Hoops did in style, overwhelming the visitors to set up a meeting with Ararat Armenia. Bradley was braced for a difficult game at the Republican Stadium in Yerevan last week. He highlighted Ararat's strength out wide, and would have noted the opposition possessed three players that were part of Armenia's 2-1 victory against the Republic of Ireland in last September's World Cup qualifier (Kamo Hovhannisyan, Artur Serobyan and Zhirayr Shaghoyan).
